quests.contextSentence: The coach asked Ms. Weiss to lend her stopwatch to the team, and they returned it after practice.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'they' is the team, so 'it' has to be the thing that was lent. That is the stopwatch, which belongs to Ms. Weiss.

quests.contextSentence: Yasmin's colleagues congratulated her on the promotion and offered to take her out for lunch.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Her' is singular, so the plural colleagues are out. The person being congratulated and taken out is Yasmin.
quests.nativeTip: Who is being taken out for lunch?

quests.contextSentence: The instructor handed the swimmers their lane numbers and told them to warm up by themselves.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'themselves' is plural and reflexive. The people told to warm up alone are the swimmers, not the instructor who is giving the instruction.

quests.contextSentence: The council promised the residents that it would repair the road after they submitted a petition.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'They' is plural and is what triggers the promise. The residents make the petition; the council is 'it'.

quests.contextSentence: Ms. Petrova invited Mr. Cole to the launch and asked him to bring his colleagues, since she wanted the whole team there.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'She' is feminine, so it cannot be Mr. Cole. The person who invites and asks is Ms. Petrova.
quests.nativeTip: Who is inviting and wants the team?

quests.contextSentence: The mechanic showed Mr. Okafor the worn brake pads and explained that they should be replaced before he drove any further.
quests.ruleExplanation: Consider the form of 'they': it is plural, so it refers to the pads. It cannot be either man, since neither is replaced.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'they' points back to ➔ 'the worn brake pads'

quests.contextSentence: The waiters set the tables while the cook prepared the sauce, and they finished before the doors opened.
quests.ruleExplanation: In this sentence, 'they' is plural, which excludes the cook. The tables are plural but are things being set; the waiters did the work.
quests.nativeTip: 'They' is plural. Who does the finishing?

quests.contextSentence: Hiro forgot to charge his phone, so he asked his roommate to lend him a charger and ended up using hers.
quests.ruleExplanation: Note that 'hers' is feminine, so it cannot be Hiro's. It stands for 'her charger', the one he borrowed from his roommate.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'hers' points back to ➔ 'his roommate's charger'

quests.contextSentence: Ms. Moreau reminded her tenants that their rent was due and that she would collect it on Wednesday.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' is singular and non-human, so it cannot be her tenants. What she will collect on Wednesday is the rent.

quests.contextSentence: The bank told Mrs. Ahmed that it could not approve the loan, so she asked it to review her file.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'her' is feminine and possessive, so it belongs to Mrs. Ahmed. The bank is 'it', not 'her'.

quests.contextSentence: The two receptionists shared the phone, and the owner told them to keep it charged.
quests.ruleExplanation: Here, 'it' is singular, so it cannot be the two receptionists. The phone is what needs charging.

quests.contextSentence: The chairman thanked the members for their patience and promised to consider their suggestions himself.
quests.ruleExplanation: Here, 'himself' is masculine and singular, so the plural members are out. It emphasises that the chairman will do this personally.
quests.nativeTip: Who will consider the suggestions personally?

quests.contextSentence: The heating engineer told Mrs. Ortiz and her husband that he would replace the boiler if they signed the quote.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'They' is plural, so it cannot be the heating engineer, who is 'he'. The people who must sign are the couple.
quests.nativeTip: Who has to sign the quote?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'they' points back to ➔ 'Mrs. Ortiz and her husband'

quests.contextSentence: Zainab asked the caretaker to open the storage room, but he said he had lent its key to the cleaners.
quests.ruleExplanation: In this sentence, 'its' is non-human. A room has a key, while the caretaker would be 'his' and the cleaners 'their'.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'its' points back to ➔ 'the storage room'

quests.contextSentence: The agent told the buyers the asking price was flexible and that he could lower it if they made an offer.
quests.ruleExplanation: Note that 'it' is singular and non-human, so it is not the buyers. What the agent can lower is the price.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'it' points back to ➔ 'the asking price'

quests.contextSentence: Mr. Kang's landlord told him that the building was being sold and that his lease would end in June.
quests.ruleExplanation: A lease is held by the tenant, not the landlord. 'His' therefore refers back to 'him', who is Mr. Kang.
quests.nativeTip: 'Him' and 'his' point to the same person. Who has a lease?

quests.contextSentence: The union rep told the workers she would raise their complaints with the board, which had cut its own budget last year.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'which' points to the board, and 'its own budget' returns to that same board. People would be 'her' or 'their'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Its' follows 'which'. What did 'which' point back to?

quests.contextSentence: The children told their babysitter that they had already tidied the room, but she wanted to see it herself.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'she' is the babysitter, and 'herself' returns to that subject. It stresses that she will look personally instead of relying on the children.

quests.contextSentence: The organisers thanked the sponsors for their generosity and told the volunteers that they would receive certificates.
quests.ruleExplanation: People are thanked for their own generosity. The sponsors are the group who gave, so 'their' refers to them.

quests.contextSentence: The doctor told the parents that their son should rest, and that he would call them if the results changed.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'he' is singular and masculine, so it could be the doctor or the son. Only the doctor has the results and would call the parents.

quests.contextSentence: Although the regulator had warned the banks that it would act if they ignored the new rules, they carried on as before.
quests.ruleExplanation: Note that 'it' is singular, so the plural banks are out. The party issuing a warning and able to act is the regulator.
quests.nativeTip: 'It' is singular. Which noun can act to enforce something?

quests.contextSentence: The site manager told the residents that he would fix the fence himself, provided they let him in.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'himself' is masculine singular, so the residents are out. The site manager is the one promising to do the work personally.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'himself' points back to ➔ 'the site manager'

quests.contextSentence: The designers sent the client two logo options and asked her to choose one, but she wanted them both revised.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Them' is plural, and 'both' points to the two things being counted. The two logo options are what she wanted revised.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'them' points back to ➔ 'the two logo options'

quests.contextSentence: The trainer told the rookies that the veterans would help them, but that they would have to learn the routines for themselves.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Them' and 'they' both point to the rookies, who need help and must learn. 'Themselves' returns to those learners.

quests.contextSentence: The instructor reminded the trainees that whoever forgot a helmet would have to sit out, and that she would not lend hers.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Hers' is feminine and stands for 'her helmet'. Since 'she' is the instructor, the helmet is the instructor's.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'hers' points back to ➔ 'the instructor's helmet'

quests.contextSentence: Tessa's parents told her uncle they would host the party if he handled the catering himself.
quests.ruleExplanation: Notice that 'himself' is singular and masculine, so the plural parents are out. He is the one who must do the catering personally.
quests.nativeTip: Who has to handle the catering?

quests.contextSentence: The website warns customers that it may reject payments if they enter their details incorrectly.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' is singular and is the subject of 'reject'. The website does the rejecting, while the customers are 'they'.
quests.nativeTip: Who or what may reject payments?

quests.contextSentence: When the surgeon told the anaesthetist he wanted the patient monitored closely, she adjusted the equipment herself.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'herself' is feminine, so it cannot be the male surgeon. It refers to the anaesthetist, who adjusted the equipment personally.
quests.nativeTip: 'He' is the surgeon. Who is the 'she' who adjusted the equipment?

quests.contextSentence: Both sisters said they would collect the tickets, but their brother had already picked them up for the whole family.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'them' is plural, so it could be the sisters. But what a brother 'picks up' for the family is the tickets.

quests.contextSentence: The company told its suppliers that it would only pay invoices that they had submitted through the new portal.
quests.ruleExplanation: In this sentence, 'they' is plural and is the subject of 'had submitted'. The company pays, whereas the suppliers are the ones who submit.
